comment: One row for each event of fir.shadow (src/fort/fir/shadow.ft, spec/ownership-design.md 3.4),
for a boundary of each, for the tags of 3.3, and for each step of the derivation of D10.7
that the event `forged` reads, with the interpreter lines that feed them
(src/fort/fir/interpreter.ft). A row names the line that decides the rule and a text that
breaks it. The first stage runs the suite of the shadow (test/fort/fir/shadow_test.ft), the
second the driver suite of --fir-events and the pass `run`, and the third the FIR tests. The
table runs in the Linux VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads
the product compiler, whose interpreter calls fir.shadow. The first round of a run can read
stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first row is one that a full run caught.

stages.name: the suite of fir.shadow
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 fir/shadow_test

stages.name: the driver suite
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_run_test
